newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN top energy officials' annual meet kicks off.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN top energy officials' annual meet kicks off.

text.p: ASEAN senior energy officials on Monday began a four-day annual meeting expected to discuss further plans on a regional gas pipeline and electricity grid.
Philippine Energy Secretary Francisco Viray said a joint statement will be issued by the energy ministers on July 2 after the two-day closed-door meetings of the senior officials.
"We still don't know exactly what the joint statement will say as this will depend on the senior officials' recommendations," Viray told reporters.

The meeting may take up changes to be endorsed to previous agreements such as the ASEAN Petroleum Security Agreement to include the new ASEAN members, Viray said. Under this agreement, oil exporting member nations committed to supply in times of shortage in the region.
Energy officials of new ASEAN members Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos came as observers to the meeting.
In last year's meeting, ASEAN ministers encouraged the private sector to participate in the trans-ASEAN gas pipeline system which has been found feasible.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
